decision.detail: I stand up from the table. Rita and Larry are still mid-sentence. I push my chair back. I walk to the coat-check, take the envelope marked CREW RETURN FARES, drop it in my inside pocket. I walk to the front door, step out into the six-a-mcold, follow the diesel smell to the curb. The van is there. The driver is on the hood of his car, hands on the wheel, looking at the flat. I don't say anything. I walk to the trunk, pull out the jack and the wrench and the spare. I get under the car. I put my shoulder to the jack. I turn the wrench four times, four lugs. I pull the flat. I slide the spare on. I turn the lugs back. I drop the car. I put the jack in the trunk. I wipe my hands on my jeans. They're black from the grease. I walk back to the lobby. I sit down. The coffee is still warm.
decision.intention: Put my hands on a tire. Get the grease under my nails. Be a body that does a thing with its arms and its back and doesn't need anyone to hear it do it. Twenty minutes of wrenching so that the afternoon isn't a plan I narrate to a payphone or a booth. Then I walk back, I sit, I drink the coffee, and I go to the coach. Pittsburgh. The couch. My sister's hallway. Wednesday. That's all. That's the whole thing.
